bio: Research physical scientist in NASA Goddard's Atmospheric Chemistry and Dynamics branch who leads the Pandora Project and the GCAS Lab. name: Ellen D. Ketterson
research_interests: phenotypic engineering; testosterone and life-history evolution; dark-eyed junco; extra-pair mating and parental behavior; avian migration timing and site fidelity
bio: Distinguished Professor Emerita of Biology at Indiana University Bloomington. Her lab manipulates hormones in free-living dark-eyed juncos ('phenotypic engineering') to learn how selection shapes integrated life histories, tracing testosterone's effects on behavior, physiology and reproductive success, and has also examined what controls migration timing, distance and site fidelity.

An ecohydrologist, he examines how cropping systems shape evapotranspiration, soil water and groundwater in the Corn Belt, and how these agroecosystems cope with drought and very wet periods.
